conviction_note: The positive lean rests on two things. The EPS bar ($0.03-0.05 across four sources) sits far below what the company's own filings imply (about $0.08-0.11), and the shareholder base is crowded and bearish: 3 of 3 analysts at Sell with $3.70-4.50 targets against a $6.05 spot, about 8% of Class A short and 7.8 days to cover. That lean is held at p_up 57, not higher, for three reasons: the Q3'25 print sold off 5.2% on a 2.5x EPS beat because revenue growth and the holiday tone disappointed; products must jump about 23% q/q to meet management's own 'H2 growth' claim; and the stock is already up about 36% since late July. abs_move is 8, between the 5.2% median and the 11.3% mean absolute reaction, because coverage is thin and the short is crowded. impact_sum (+1.8) and the scaled number (+1.12) agree in sign; the gap is the reaction-function discount carried in p_up.

positioning_check: Short interest was 4,411,918 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, down from 5,712,516 on 2026-07-15. Days to cover were 7.8 on 565k average daily volume (https://equibles.com/stocks/crct/short-interest). That is about 2.1% of the 209m total shares but about 7.7-8.1% of the Class A float (54.7m Class A shares per the Q2 10-Q cover page, 57.6m per Blasnik's 13G), so the short is moderately crowded and has been covering. There is no usable option chain (baseline options.status empty_chain), so there is no skew signal. Sell-side: 3 analysts, all Sell or Strong Sell, targets $3.70/$4.00/$4.50, about 33% below spot; the last action was Barclays maintaining Sell at $4 on 2026-09-10 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crct/forecast/). The run-up was -5.2% over 20 days and -1.6% over 5 days, but the stock sits 9.7% below its 52-week high and 62% above its low, up from about $4.45 on 2026-07-26 (Trefis) to $6.05.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is $0.03-0.05 in four estimate sources against Q3'25 actual $0.10. The company's own filings point to roughly $0.08-0.11. Underlying Q2'26 gross margin, after removing the $17.9m IEEPA refund and the $6.4m royalty-settlement release, was about 58.9% (Q1'26 58.1%), against 55.2% in Q3'25 when IEEPA tariffs were still charged. Q2'26 opex was about $69m. Management said 'we expect to be profitable each quarter' and guided platform growth every quarter. On about $170m of revenue and $72-75m of opex that gives roughly $22-28m of operating income. This sell-side has under-forecast EPS by 1.5-4x in each of the last eight quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats came every quarter but were bought unevenly. Q3'25: $0.10 vs $0.04 with a revenue beat, and the stock fell 5.19% on revenue growth and holiday caution. Q2'26: $0.19 vs $0.05 including one-offs, with a revenue miss, and it rose 22.87%. Q1'26: $0.10 vs $0.057, +5.21%. Q4'25: $0.04 vs $0.03, +4.63% (baseline history; https://ca.investing.com/equities/cricut-earnings).
findings.why_not_priced: Three Sell-rated analysts have kept EPS near $0.04 through eight beats. If the market priced a ~$0.10 quarter on a $1.25bn market cap, the sell-side targets would not sit 33% below spot and short interest would not still be ~8% of the Class A float. The stock's move since July is consistent with partial pricing, so this is filed as a lean, not a lock.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828962/000182896226000048/cricutq22026earningsrelease.htm) and the call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) are the same company disclosure set. The consensus figures come from separate aggregators. This is an inference from company documents, not a disclosed Q3 number.

findings.finding: Q3 products revenue has to rise about 23% q/q to meet management's 'H2 products growth' claim: Q3'25 products were $87.7m and Q2'26 were $71.3m (-22% y/y). Supporting it: Maker 5 launched 2026-09-04 at $349+ bundles with a two-week Cricut.com/Michaels exclusive and was reportedly out of stock on 2026-09-05. Management also said the Q2 Europe distribution timing gap is not a Q3 headwind. Against it: the launch gives less than one month of the quarter, there were continued promotions on Maker 4 and Joy Xtra, and accessories and materials keep eroding. Platform at about +5% adds roughly $4m. Net, total revenue lands at roughly $165-176m, inside a disputed $164-177m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 fell 5.19% when 'Q3 revenue growth disappointed' (https://www.itiger.com/news/1128325695), even with an EPS beat. Q2'26 rose 22.87% despite a 22% products decline and a revenue miss. Q4'24 rose 4.21% on a revenue miss. So the revenue line has been both punished and ignored.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue consensus spans 7% across sources, so no single bar is priced. If the market expected a clear products return to growth, the high-end estimates ($176.6m) would be the consensus and the sell-side would have moved off Sell after the launch. Barclays maintained Sell at $4 on 2026-09-10, after the launch.
findings.independence: The launch stock-out report is a separate source (https://www.thecraftycatsman.com/news/cricut-maker-5-launch-2026/), and Kohl's lists Maker 5 bundles at 4.6/5 from 98 reviews (https://www.kohls.com/product/prd-8711913/cricut-maker-5-essential-bundle-cutting-machine.jsp). The management claim comes from the call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The bar is disputed, so this is capped small.

findings.finding: Paid-subscriber growth has slowed to +3% y/y (3.10m in Q2'26, +25k q/q) from +6% in Q3'25. Management pre-flagged that subscriber trends soften in Q3 on seasonality, and it is testing higher iOS pricing for new subscribers. A flat or down sequential subscriber count is likely but was already told to the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3'25, subscribers were +6% but active users were flat and 90-day engaged users were -3%; the stock fell 5.19% (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35901592/cricut-inc-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results).
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: management guided it. It is filed because a sequential decline in the paid base would be the first since the subscription tiers changed, and the stock's run since July has not been tested on a subscriber print.
findings.independence: The Q1'26 call coverage on the pricing test (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cricut-q1-earnings-call-highlights-234318591.html) is a separate source.

findings.finding: Margin headwinds the company itself disclosed: the Q2 10-Q says Cricut is 'beginning to experience supply-chain cost pressure related to the Middle East conflict' (fuel and petrochemical inputs; vinyl and materials are petrochemical). The call added possible gross-margin pressure from ramping AI features and a marketing ramp in H2. Existing non-IEEPA tariffs remain a headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4'25, management flagged gross-margin pressure from tariffs and promotions; the stock rose 4.63% on a small beat. Margin warnings have not been punished on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely inside what the company told the market, and the $0.03-0.05 EPS consensus already embeds heavy margin compression. It is filed small because the magnitude of the Middle East cost pressure is not quantified anywhere.
findings.independence: This shares the 10-Q with the EPS finding, which is already sized net of these headwinds. The transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) carries the AI and marketing comments.

findings.finding: Residual IEEPA refund flow: $1.7m of refunds booked against inventory will reach cost of revenue as that inventory sells through. A $3.5m refund receivable was open at 2026-06-30, and the CFO said 'there are still some that we're working' beyond the large majority already received. That is a small one-off tailwind to Q3 gross margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2'26 refund-boosted quarter rose 22.87%, but that print also carried a $17.9m refund. Here the amount is a tenth of that and has no path to guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Too small for aggregators to model. It is a one-off below the line the stock trades on, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: The transcript confirms the remaining refunds (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/11/cricut-crct-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Same company disclosure set.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Cricut signed a new 5-year $300m senior secured multicurrency revolver with BMO, replacing the undrawn 2022 JPMorgan facility. It sets no dollar limit on dividends or buybacks while pro forma net leverage is at or below 2.5x, and allows the leverage cap to step up to 3.5x after a permitted acquisition over $75m. What the money buys: nothing visible needs funding. The company is debt-free with $267m cash and $19m securities, so this is capacity for capital return or M&A, not a ramp and not distress. The buyback authorization has only $21.6m left, and the semi-annual $0.10 dividend has historically been declared around the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital-return announcements (special dividends of $0.40 in May 2024 and $0.75 in May 2025) came with Q1 prints that rose 20.32% (May 2025). No Q3 print has carried a special dividend.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a quiet 8-K that no wire covered. If the market read it as a signal of a buyback replenishment or special dividend, it would show in previews, and none mention it. The positive read is not corroborated by any stated use, so it stays small.
findings.independence: The dividend history (FY2025 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1828962/000182896226000010/crct-20251231.htm) shows the board's pattern but says no dividend policy is adopted. Separate document.

findings.finding: The positioning is bearish into the print. All three covering analysts rate Sell or Strong Sell, with targets $3.70-4.50 (about 33% below the $6.05 spot). Short interest is 4.41m shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 8% of the ~55-58m Class A float, with 7.8 days to cover. Six of the last seven prints rose, three of them by 17-23%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reactions: +22.87, +5.21, +4.63, -5.19, +16.91, +20.32, +4.21 (baseline). The only decline was a Q3 print.
findings.why_not_priced: The short has been covering (5.71m in July to 4.41m in October) while the stock rose about 36%, so part of the fuel is spent. What remains is a 7.8-day cover on a thinly traded float against a low EPS bar. If this were fully priced, short interest would have fallen further and the sell-side would have moved targets toward spot.
findings.independence: The analyst targets come from a separate source (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crct/forecast/). The Class A share count comes from the 10-Q cover page and the 13G.

findings.finding: CEO Ashish Arora sold 180,000 Class A shares on 2026-10-21 to 10-23 at about $6.26-6.32 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-08-20, leaving 4.91m direct. Form 144s and Form 4s recur every two to four weeks from August through October, which reads as a routine plan, not a signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no record of this stock reacting to insider plan sales.
findings.why_not_priced: Public on EDGAR, and a pre-scheduled plan, so it is near zero by construction.
findings.independence: The EDGAR submissions list shows the cadence of Form 144s and Form 4s (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001828962.json).

findings.finding: Steven Blasnik filed a Schedule 13G for 2,930,714 Class A shares (5.09% of Class A) with an event date of 2026-09-21. A new disclosed long holder of a thin float is accumulating ahead of the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a passive 13G on a controlled company, with no wire coverage. It only matters as float absorption into a crowded short.

findings.finding: Etsy, the closest public read on the handmade and craft consumer, reported Q3 2026 marketplace GMS +8.8% y/y. Active buyers rose by about 540k sequentially and gross buyer additions grew 6.2%, so the crafting and DIY consumer was not weakening in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured relation between CRCT reactions and Etsy prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Etsy reported after Cricut last spoke, and CRCT analysts have not updated since 2026-09-10. It is a proxy: Etsy sellers are partly Cricut users, but the transmission is unconfirmed, so it is filed small.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not company data. Separate coverage: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3018920/etsy-q3-earnings-beat-estimates-on-gms-ads-growth-revenues-rise-yy

baseline_tension: There is no option skew to agree or disagree with. The positive lean agrees with the reaction history (6 of 7 up) and cuts against the sell-side targets. Its main tension is the roughly 36% run since late July into a 52-week-high zone, which moves p_up toward 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Q3'25 sold off 5.2% on a 2.5x EPS beat, so the EPS-bar finding was cut from +2.0 to +1.5 and p_up from 58 to 57.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): asked what the revolver buys. The answer was no corroborated use, only capacity for capital return or M&A on a debt-free balance sheet, so it was cut from +0.3 to +0.2 and kept positive.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): the Etsy GMS proxy was cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the residual refund was cut from +0.2 to +0.1, with no path to guidance.
Lesson 6 (bar): the revenue bar is disputed ($164-177m) and stays capped small on the products finding. The EPS bar has four agreeing sources and was left standing.
Lessons 7 and 8 left the positioning finding (+0.8) and abs_move (8) unchanged.
